items.title: I built a memory tool for Claude Code that never leaves your disk
items.why_it_matters: A developer built "deposition," a local memory tool designed specifically for Claude Code that keeps your project context on your own disk. Since you use Claude Code daily, this solves the issue of the AI forgetting your project's rules and architecture between terminal sessions. This week, clone the repo and hook it up to your local environment to keep your AI-ingest rules persistently active during your build sessions.

items.title: Show HN: SightDiff – before/after visual proof of what your AI agent changed
items.why_it_matters: SightDiff provides visual before-and-after proof of what your AI agent changed in your frontend. Since you are vibe coding your Next.js app and letting the AI handle the keyboard, this helps you instantly verify visual changes and catch UI regressions without manual hunting. This week, run SightDiff on your next Next.js layout change to see exactly what Claude modified before you commit.

items.title: Show HN: Neal – Claude and Codex working together
items.why_it_matters: A developer shipped Neal, a CLI orchestrator that coordinates Claude and Codex as planner, coder, and reviewer roles to prevent context rot on large tasks. This is a great blueprint for how to transition from a basic prompter to a director who orchestrates different models for different tasks. This week, look at their system prompts in the GitHub repo and try manually splitting your next feature request into a "planner" phase and a "coder" phase.

items.title: Show HN: My Claude subscription did $5,868 of API-equivalent work last month
items.why_it_matters: A developer built a tool to track how much API-equivalent work their Claude Pro subscription is doing, revealing they got $5,868 worth of value in a single month. This is a great utility for understanding the economics of your development setup as you scale your usage. This week, run this script against your own Claude history to audit your usage and see how much value you are extracting from your subscription.

items.title: Show HN: Markleft – how I review Claude's Markdown plans
items.why_it_matters: Markleft is a lightweight tool built to review and parse Markdown plans generated by Claude before they are executed. Since your primary role is directing the AI and verifying its plans, this tool helps you catch structural errors before the AI starts writing code. This week, paste Claude's next implementation plan into Markleft to review and prune the steps before letting Claude Code touch your codebase.
